excerpt_i18n.en:
In cardiovascular disease prevention, a long-standing challenge is that many conditions remain latent in the body for years before onset, making it difficult to accurately predict early on whether an individual will face multiple cardiovascular disease risks simultaneously. Traditional risk assessments have primarily relied on conventional clinical indicators such as age, blood pressure, and lipid levels, or polygenic risk scores. However, cardiovascular diseases often involve a long-term evolution with multiple potential outcomes, making it hard for single indicators or disease-specific prediction methods to fully capture the true risk.

With advances in large-scale population cohorts and high-throughput molecular detection technologies, researchers have found that proteins and metabolites in the blood can more directly reflect the body’s current physiological state and disease progression. These molecular signals are influenced not only by genetic factors but also by environmental and lifestyle changes, providing new sources of information for long-term risk assessment.

Against this backdrop, a research team led by Associate Professor Zhang Qingpeng from the University of Hong Kong’s Data Science Institute and Department of Pharmacology and Pharmacy conducted a study integrating multiomics information with artificial intelligence, based on large-scale prospective population data from the UK Biobank. Moving beyond the "one disease, one model" approach, the team incorporated proteomic and metabolomic information into a unified framework to simultaneously assess long-term risks for multiple cardiovascular diseases. Las evaluaciones de riesgo tradicionales se basan principalmente en indicadores clínicos convencionales como edad, presión arterial y niveles de lípidos, o en puntuaciones de riesgo genético poligénico. Sin embargo, las enfermedades cardiovasculares suelen evolucionar a largo plazo y pueden presentar múltiples desenlaces simultáneos, por lo que un único indicador o un enfoque predictivo centrado en una sola enfermedad difícilmente refleja el riesgo real de manera integral. excerpt_i18n.zh: 就在昨天，阶跃星辰登顶了全球模型榜单——他们最新开源的 Agent 基座模型 Step 3.5 Flash，发布首日便登上全球模型平台OpenRouter 的 “最快模型榜”，而发布后仅用短短两天，就获得了OpenRouter“热度趋势榜”排名第一的好成绩，其数据是基于全球开发者与用户的实际模型调用量。也就是说，Step 3.5 Flash以硬实力赢得了用户的“用脚投票”。 （图为Step 3.5 Flash 登顶 OpenRouter 的Trending 榜单） 对阶跃来说，拿下榜单第一并不新鲜，而这个成绩有意思的地方在于，它点破了当前AI应用深化的一个普遍瓶颈：模型越来越“聪明”，能处理的任务越来越复杂，但用户和开发者在真实使用时，最直接的感官体验却是——“慢”。 这里的“慢”，不是指回答一句“你好”的速度，而是当用户任务变得复杂，任务链和工作流明显变长（比如分析整篇财报、编写复杂函数、或同时完成图文音视频多模态输出等等）时，AI的处理速度必然下降，用户的等待时间可能会被拖得很长。 漫长的等待——本身就严重限制了 AI 在实际工作流中的可用性；而如果等了半天，AI 拿出的结果还不能令人满意，用户的流失就已成定局。 而过去外界的一贯认知中，“快”=小参数模型的敏捷调用、输出；“慢”=更大参数量级的模型和细致的思考。此前，模型要的是“快”和“好”的平衡，而今天，阶跃的Step 3.5 Flash 却敢于对世界说：“我全都要！” 稀疏 MoE 架构：不要“大而全”，我要“以巧见大” 论速度，Step 3.5 Flash 有多快？ 在复杂推理场景下，保证稳定性的同时，Step 3.5 Flash 在 NVDIA Hopper GPU&nbs
excerpt_i18n.en: Just yesterday, StepFun topped the global model rankings—their newly open-sourced Agent base model Step 3.5 Flash reached the top of the "Fastest Models" chart on the global model platform OpenRouter on its release day. Within just two days of its launch, it secured the number one spot on OpenRouter's "Trending" chart, based on actual model call volumes from developers and users worldwide. In other words, Step 3.5 Flash earned users' "vote with their feet" through solid performance. (Image: Step 3.5 Flash topping OpenRouter's Trending chart) For StepFun, topping the charts is nothing new, but what makes this achievement interesting is that it highlights a common bottleneck in the deepening of AI applications: models are becoming increasingly "smarter" and capable of handling more complex tasks, yet the most direct sensory experience for users and developers in real-world use is "slowness." This "slowness" does not refer to the speed of answering a simple "hello," but rather when user tasks become complex, with significantly longer task chains and workflows (such as analyzing an entire financial report, writing complex functions, or simultaneously completing multimodal outputs of text, images, audio, and video, etc.), the AI's processing speed inevitably decreases, and users' waiting time may be dragged out considerably.
